name: Maxeon SPR MAX6 425W
notes: Technology: IBC (interdigitated back contact) cells, 66-cell, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, in two finishes. Runs 425-440W. Pros: IBC eliminates front grid lines and reduces micro-cracking, and the white-backsheet 440W bin is the outright performance leader with higher current for the same cell technology; Maxeon backs it with a 40-year warranty if registered. Cons: among the most expensive panels per watt on the market by a wide margin, and the all-black 425W bin trades a little current for its darker backsheet's heat profile.

name: Maxeon SPR MAX7 435W
notes: Technology: IBC (interdigitated back contact) cells, 112-cell Maxeon Gen 7 platform, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, white backsheet. Runs 435-445W - the direct successor to the SPR MAX6 series. Pros: efficiency climbs to 24.1% (vs 22.8% for MAX6's best bin), and it carries the same industry-leading 40-year product and performance warranty (98% minimum output in year 1, max 0.25%/yr degradation). Cons: among the most expensive panels per watt on the market; Maxeon Solar Technologies has been through corporate restructuring since 2025-2026, so it's worth confirming with a supplier that UK stock and warranty backing are currently secure before specifying it.

name: Maxeon SPR MAX3 410W
notes: Technology: IBC (interdigitated back contact) cells, 112-cell Maxeon Gen 3 platform, monofacial with single 3.2mm glass, in two finishes. Runs 410-430W - the direct predecessor to the SPR MAX6 series, and Maxeon's more affordable residential IBC option. Pros: IBC's usual advantages of no front grid lines and reduced micro-cracking, and Maxeon backs it with a 40-year warranty if registered. Cons: among the most expensive panels per watt on the market despite being Maxeon's cheaper tier, and its efficiency (up to 22.7%) trails the newer MAX6 and MAX7 platforms.
